candidates.spoken: Why a planet 95 times Earth's mass could float.
Saturn is about 30% less dense than water.
What If You Put Saturn in a Bathtub?
Would Saturn Really Float in Water?
Saturn were placed in an enormous bathtub.
On average density alone it would float.
It would not all happen at once.
Its average density is just 0.69 grams per cubic centimetre.
It spreads its mass across a radius about 9 times Earth's.
On average, it's an eighth as dense as Earth.
It has an eighth of the average density of Earth.
In reality, a ball of gas would fall apart first.
So the ringed giant is mostly light gas, stretched thin.
In a big enough bathtub, it would, in principle, float.
An object floats if its average density is lower than the fluid's.
